% Pattern: kind/title-prefix. The environment writes its title and then its
% argument, as "{\bf \theitem.\hspace{1em}Theorem#1.}", and the argument only
% adds to the title: a label, a citation or a letter. Each use is a theorem.
% Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want theo-1 statement/theorem 1.1 status=here
% want pf-1 proof - proves=theo-1 flags=
% want theo-2 statement/theorem 1.2 status=none
\documentclass{article}
\newcounter{item}[section]
\renewcommand{\theitem}{\arabic{section}.\arabic{item}}
\newenvironment{theo}[1]{\refstepcounter{item}\par
\indent {\bf \theitem.\hspace{1em}Theorem#1.} \sl }{\par}
\newenvironment{pf}{\par\indent {\bf Proof.} }{ $\Box$\par}
\begin{document}
\section{One}
\begin{theo}{\label{a}} Every compact space is bounded. \end{theo}
\begin{pf} Cover the space by balls. \end{pf}
\begin{theo}{\cite{ref}} A closed part of a compact space is compact. \end{theo}
\end{document}
